american-petroleum-institute.text: The American Petroleum Institute (API) is the main U.S. trade association for the oil and natural gas industry. It was formed in 1919 and has about 600 members. At API's 1959 'Energy and Man' symposium marking the industry's centennial, physicist Edward Teller warned that carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels could warm the planet, and a 1968 Stanford Research Institute report commissioned by API warned of significant temperature changes by 2000. In 1998, a group that included API, Exxon, Chevron and Southern Company drafted a communications plan stating: 'Victory will be achieved when average citizens understand uncertainties in climate science.'

bcci.text: The Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) was an international bank founded in 1972 by Pakistani banker Agha Hasan Abedi, with Abu Dhabi's ruling family as founding and majority shareholders. A December 1992 report to the U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Committee by Senators John Kerry and Hank Brown found that BCCI operated in 73 countries through a structure designed to evade regulation. The report documented fraud, money laundering, bribery and support of arms trafficking, and found that the CIA used BCCI and its secretly owned U.S. subsidiary First American for operations. BCCI was closed by regulators on July 5, 1991.

bis.text: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) was established in 1930 in Basel, Switzerland, under the Young Plan to manage German First World War reparation payments. It describes itself as the world's oldest international financial institution and is owned by 63 central banks. During the Second World War it continued to receive interest payments, mostly in gold, from the German Reichsbank. It also received 3.7 tonnes of gold that had been looted from the central banks of Belgium and the Netherlands, which it returned in 1948. The BIS hosts the secretariat of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, which sets international bank capital standards.

credit-suisse.text: Credit Suisse was a Swiss global bank. In March 2021 it lost $5.5 billion when Archegos Capital Management, Bill Hwang's family office, defaulted on margin calls; an independent review attributed the loss to a 'fundamental failure of management and controls' in its investment bank. In March 2023, after a crisis of confidence and large client outflows, UBS took over Credit Suisse with support from the Swiss Confederation, the Swiss National Bank and FINMA. As part of the deal, FINMA ordered a complete write-down of about CHF 16 billion of Credit Suisse's Additional Tier 1 (AT1) bonds.

darpa.text: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is the research and development agency of the U.S. Department of Defense, created in response to the Soviet Union's 1957 Sputnik launch. DARPA credits its work with leading to the modern internet (via ARPANET), GPS receivers small enough for consumer devices, and automated voice recognition and translation. In January 2002 it established the Information Awareness Office under retired Admiral John Poindexter to develop data-mining and analysis tools for a prototype counterterrorism system called Total Information Awareness (TIA). Congress cut off TIA's funding in 2003 after privacy objections.

He has said Thiel called him there to tell him about Confinity. He joined in November 1999 and ran product (most recently as Executive Vice President of Product). imf.text: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is an international financial institution conceived at the July 1944 Bretton Woods conference, with 191 member countries. Each member's quota reflects its size in the world economy and determines its voting power and access to IMF resources. IMF lending is conditional: borrowing governments agree to adjust economic policies, with commitments ranging from fiscal and reserve targets to structural reforms, and funds are typically disbursed in installments tied to those actions.

lehman-brothers.text: Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy on September 15, 2008. With $639 billion in consolidated assets, it was the largest financial bankruptcy in U.S. history and a central event of the 2008 financial crisis. The court-appointed examiner, Anton Valukas, issued a roughly 2,200-page report in 2010. It found that Lehman used 'Repo 105' transactions to temporarily remove up to about $50 billion of securities from its balance sheet at quarter-ends to lower its reported net leverage, without disclosing the practice, and that there were colorable claims against senior executives and its auditor.
